name: PURGE
description:
PURGE: Partition-Aware Unlearning for Removing Spurious-Correlation Generated Errors
	

PURGE is a partitioning strategy applied to existing public datasets (MSCOCO 2017) that separates object-relevant evidence from spurious background cues in LVLMs. This repository hosts the resulting preprocessed retain/forget partitions for direct reuse.
NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track, Submission #2701.

citeAs: @inproceedings{sarker2026purge, title={Partition-Aware Unlearning for Removing Spurious Correlations in Large Vision-Language Models}, author={Sarker, Aditi and Shah, Nazreen and Sultan, Rafi Ibn and Jang, Rhongho and Zhu, Dongxiao and Khanduri, Prashant}, booktitle={The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year={2026}, url={https://openreview.net/forum?id=Tt3sSoAeJd}}
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for research on diagnosing and mitigating spurious object-background correlations in large vision-language models, including benchmarking hallucination-related metrics (CHAIR, POPE, AMBER, MMHal-Bench) and developing/evaluating unlearning-based mitigation methods (e.g. Gradient Ascent, KL-based, NPO objectives). Not intended for training production-grade object detectors or as a general-purpose replacement for MSCOCO.
rai:dataLimitations: As stated in the paper's Limitations section: PURGE's partitions depend on the quality of masks, counterfactual images, cue proposals, and detector outputs, and effectiveness may decrease when object and background cues are highly entangled; constructing the partitions adds data-processing overhead relative to using MSCOCO directly. Additional scope limitations: the dataset is restricted to MSCOCO's 80 object categories and MSCOCO's image distribution (2014 collection, predominantly English-language contexts and captions); PURGE-H partitions are specific to the LVLM used to generate them (LLaVA-1.6-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, or Qwen3.5-9B) and are not guaranteed to transfer as retain/forget labels for a different model; the PURGE-D inpainting variant may itself introduce inpainting-model artifacts as a secondary distribution shift. Not recommended as a general-purpose replacement for MSCOCO or as a source of ground-truth object detection labels beyond what MSCOCO already provides.
rai:dataBiases: Inherits any photographic, geographic, and object-category biases present in MSCOCO train2017 (e.g., over-representation of common Western/English-language photo-sharing contexts, since MSCOCO images originate from Flickr). Additionally, PURGE-H retain/forget labels inherit any biases of the specific LVLM used to generate them (LLaVA-1.6-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, or Qwen3.5-9B); PURGE-M retain/forget labels inherit any biases of the language model used for cue proposal and the open-vocabulary detector used for cue scoring (following the SpurLens methodology); and the PURGE-D inpainting variant inherits any biases of the GMCNN inpainting model (Wang et al., 2018). None of these component models' own bias characteristics are re-audited within this paper.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to reduce hallucination and spurious-correlation failures in LVLMs, which can improve reliability in downstream applications; misuse risk is considered low as the dataset only repackages existing public MSCOCO imagery for diagnostic/research purposes.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: MSCOCO images may contain incidental depictions of people in public scenes (as in the original MSCOCO dataset); no additional personal or sensitive information is collected, and no attempt is made to identify individuals. No PII, health, or demographic labels are added by PURGE.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Preprocessing: object regions are identified from MSCOCO instance bounding boxes. PURGE-D masks these regions to isolate object vs. background pixels (default variant); a secondary variant additionally inpaints the masked regions using a generative multi-column CNN (GMCNN) inpainting model (Wang, Tao, Qi, Shen & Jia, 'Image inpainting via generative multi-column convolutional neural networks,' NeurIPS 2018). PURGE-H partitions images by comparing predictions from the evaluated LVLM itself (LLaVA-1.6-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, or Qwen3.5-9B, queried with a binary object-presence question) against MSCOCO ground truth, on both the original image and a counterfactual image with the target object removed. PURGE-M partitions images using MSCOCO ground-truth object presence together with a contextual cue score, computed by following the SpurLens methodology (Hosseini et al., arXiv:2503.08884, 2025) in which a language model proposes candidate co-occurring background cues and an open-vocabulary detector scores each image, thresholded to define cue presence/absence. Data collection: derived entirely from MSCOCO train2017 images (2014 collection period, MSCOCO's original geographic/source scope); no new images collected. Data annotation: no manual/crowdsourced annotation was performed for PURGE itself -- all retain/forget/partition labels are automatically derived from MSCOCO ground-truth annotations and/or model predictions as described above; see rai:dataAnnotationProtocol for the per-variant labeling logic.
rai:dataCollection: All images are derived from MSCOCO train2017 (Lin et al., 2014). PURGE-D's default construction applies bounding-box masking to an image v with object mask M(v), producing complementary object-only and background-only views (v = v⊙M(v), v = v⊙(1−M(v))); a secondary inpainting-based variant additionally fills masked regions using a generative multi-column CNN inpainting model (Wang et al., 'Image inpainting via generative multi-column convolutional neural networks,' NeurIPS 2018) to produce more natural counterfactual images (reported separately in the paper's Appendix C). PURGE-H partitions images using each evaluated LVLM's own predictions (LLaVA-1.6-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, or Qwen3.5-9B) on a binary presence question ('Is there a [object] in the image?'), compared against MSCOCO ground-truth object presence, plus the same model's prediction on a counterfactual image with the target object removed. PURGE-M partitions images using MSCOCO ground-truth object presence together with a contextual cue score computed by following the SpurLens methodology (Hosseini et al., 'SpurLens: Automatic detection of spurious cues in multimodal LLMs,' arXiv:2503.08884, 2025): a language model proposes candidate co-occurring background cues, and an open-vocabulary detector computes a per-image cue score that is thresholded to determine cue presence/absence. No new images were photographed or scraped; no human subjects were involved beyond MSCOCO's original collection.
rai:dataCollectionType: Derived/transformed from an existing public dataset (MSCOCO train2017) via automated image processing (bounding-box masking, and for one PURGE-D variant, generative inpainting) and automated model-based partitioning (LVLM prediction comparison for PURGE-H; ground-truth object presence plus detector-based cue scoring for PURGE-M). No new primary data (images) were collected.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For PURGE-M, two of the four semantic partitions (C∩S, entangled object+cue evidence, and Cc∩Sc, trivial negatives) are excluded from the training retain/forget sets, though both are retained and released for evaluation. The paper's Limitations section notes overall partition quality depends on mask, counterfactual-image, cue-proposal, and detector quality, and may degrade when object and background cues are highly entangled.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: MSCOCO train2017 images and instance annotations (https://cocodataset.org), redistributed here only as derived/masked crops under the same or a compatible license.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: PURGE-D: retain/forget views are derived directly from MSCOCO instance bounding boxes via masking (no manual annotation); no additional retain/forget label is assigned beyond the object-present vs. background-only image pair itself. PURGE-H: for each image, ground-truth object presence o in {0,1} is compared against the evaluated LVLM's prediction y-hat on the original image and on a counterfactual (object-removed) image, yielding four cells (o=1,pred=1) and (o=0,pred=0) -> retain; (o=1,pred=0) and (o=0,pred=1) -> forget. PURGE-M: images are labeled by ground-truth object presence (set C vs. Cc) crossed with a thresholded contextual-cue-presence score (set S vs. Sc, via the SpurLens-style language-model cue proposal + open-vocabulary detector scoring described in rai:dataCollection); retain = C ∩ Sc, forget = Cc ∩ S, with C ∩ S and Cc ∩ Sc released for evaluation only.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Automated pipeline (Python scripts in Dataset_creation/); no crowdsourcing or manual annotation platform was used.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All retain/forget/partition labels are deterministic functions of MSCOCO ground-truth annotations and/or automated model predictions (see rai:dataAnnotationProtocol); the paper does not describe a separate manual spot-check or human agreement study of these automatically-derived labels. Indirect validation is provided by downstream benchmark results (CHAIR, POPE, Causal-HalBench, MM-SpuBench, AMBER, MMHal-Bench) showing consistent improvements when models are unlearned on the resulting retain/forget partitions, and the paper's Limitations section explicitly notes that partition quality is bounded by the quality of the underlying masks, counterfactual images, cue proposals, and detector outputs.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be hosted at HuggingFace indefinitely; the authors will address correctness issues via versioned releases and monitor the repository's issue tracker.
